newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Saudi trade minister to take part in WTO talks.
newsitem.headline: Saudi trade minister to take part in WTO talks.

text.p: Saudi Arabia and its trading partners on Wednesday open the second round of negotiations on the oil giant's application to the World Trade Organisation (WTO), trade officials said on Tuesday.
Saudi Commerce Minister Osamah bin Jaafar bin Ibrahim Faqih will lead a large delegation to the closed-door talks being held in Geneva through Friday, according to Saudi trade envoys.
Concerns over Saudi enforcement of intellectual property rights of patents and copyright protection are likely to be voiced at Wednesday's session.
"Intellectual property is an area of concern for everyone," a trade source said.
The first round of talks on the world's largest oil exporter entering the 125-member WTO was held last May.
Faqih, in an interview with Reuters at the time, said Riyadh hoped to be admitted to the trade watchdog in 1997.

He confirmed that Saudi Arabia was seeking membership as a developing country granted a special transition period during which to conform to WTO rules in such areas as patent and copyright protection.
Saudi Arabia applied in July 1993 to the WTO's predecessor body, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT). But the GATT working party set up to study the request made no progress.
Bilateral talks with trading partners including the United States, European Union, Canada, Japan and Switzerland, are expected to be held on Thursday.
The bilateral sessions will eventually establish concessions to be put in the schedules for goods and services as part of the accession protocol.
The formal WTO talks under Canada's trade ambassador John Weekes, who chairs the working party studying the Saudi request, will resume on Friday to look at the services and goods sectors.
Last month Jordan began negotiations to become a WTO member as a developing country. Oman also has a bid under study.
In all, 31 countries have applications pending.
